title: Métricas, desbalance, calibración y umbrales
scope: LESSONS_ONLY: title/tagline/job relevance, 8 outcomes, 34/34 theory/reference paragraphs, 8 theory code/output blocks, 9 callouts and 2 figures. I Do / We Do / You Do / self-check / exams excluded.

live_status.public_card_tagline: De scores del baseline a una cola humana calibrada: métricas honestas, thr versionado y abstención — nunca autofraude
live_status.reason: The available public crawl is approximately four weeks old; do not convert the 18h vs 9h mismatch into a confirmed deployment defect without a fresh rendered read.

research_basis: scikit-learn model evaluation: AP = sum of precision weighted by recall increments; AP is not trapezoidal PR-AUC
scikit-learn probability calibration: calibrator fit must use predictions independent of base-model training; Brier mixes reliability, resolution and uncertainty
CalibratedClassifierCV: cross-validation can generate unbiased predictions for calibration
TunedThresholdClassifierCV: threshold tuning is a fitted selection step and same-data tuning is warned against
imbalanced-learn common pitfalls: resampling before split/CV creates leakage and unrealistic test distributions
StratifiedKFold preserves class proportions approximately; group constraints require group-aware splitting

runtime_counterexamples.impact: zip silently deletes the missing prediction
AP changes with input order under tied scores
caller denominator can make recall impossible
mismatched vectors can report perfect Brier
the affine calibrator can create a legal probability that vanishes from calibration analysis

runtime_counterexamples.case: affine output 0.595 rounded to two decimals before thr=0.6

runtime_counterexamples.observed: thr=.8,cost=10 while no-review cost=0 is excluded
runtime_counterexamples.impact: optimizer can force a dominated policy
invalid numerical state becomes an ordinary workflow state

findings.summary: S34 treats S33 scores as trustworthy although S33 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with baseline leakage, no fitted logistic/CV and no promotion gate.
findings.fix: Reject scores unless a machine-valid S33 run manifest is supplied.

findings.summary: No S34 metric/calibration API requires run_id, feature-set hash, split manifest, target/horizon or sample IDs.
findings.fix: Introduce PredictionRow/RunManifest lineage before evaluation.

findings.summary: Critical policies are prints/literals such as accuracy_only=False, resample_global=False, accuracy_enough=False and force_label=False, not executable gates.
findings.fix: Turn policy invariants into pytest/assertions over real functions.

findings.summary: confusion_counts and average_precision use zip without cardinality or sample-id alignment; missing rows silently disappear.
findings.fix: Require one gold and one prediction per sample_id and equal validated cardinality.

findings.summary: Binary metric helpers accept non-binary/NaN labels or predictions; invalid rows can disappear from TP/FP/FN/TN.
findings.fix: Validate finite binary domain before counting.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled AP ranks tied scores individually; AP changes with input order whereas threshold-based AP must be tie-invariant.
findings.fix: Use sklearn average_precision_score or group tied scores by threshold.

findings.summary: AP is described as an approximation to PR-AUC and ROC as inflated by many TN; both are oversimplifications that create a false metric model.
findings.fix: Define AP separately from trapezoidal PR-AUC and explain why PR metrics are often more informative under rare positives.

findings.summary: No-positive denominators collapse to metric=0 without support/undefined state.
findings.fix: Report support and zero_division/undefined status.

findings.summary: accuracy_only=False is written rather than derived, so REJECT_ACCURACY_ONLY cannot fire.
findings.fix: Validate the actual report fields.

findings.summary: precision@k/recall@k receive only preordered labels, not scores; the helper cannot prove ranking order.
findings.fix: Accept keyed score/label rows and sort inside the metric boundary.

findings.summary: k and n_pos are unvalidated; k=0 crashes, negative k yields nonsense, k>N changes denominator, and bad n_pos can make recall>1.
findings.fix: Require 1<=k<=N and derive n_pos from the eligible gold set.

findings.summary: No stable rule exists when the top-k cutoff crosses equal scores; input order can change queue precision.
findings.fix: Version a deterministic secondary key or an explicit include-all-ties policy.

findings.summary: top-k is measured on three rows while overload uses unrelated load=50/capacity=10, so the capacity evidence is disconnected from the ranked queue.
findings.fix: Derive n_review/load from the same eligible ranked rows and policy.

findings.summary: The T1-B figure talks about uncertainty, five guards, invalid_input and accept although none exists in the top-k theory/code.
findings.fix: Replace with a ranking/capacity figure or move a coherent abstention figure to T4-B.

findings.summary: apply_rebalance_in_fold does not rebalance anything and fold_plan hardcodes test_untouched=True even for resample_global=True.
findings.fix: Execute train-only weighting/resampling and make global resampling fail.

findings.summary: weight_ratio has no support/domain contract; n1=0 divides by zero.
findings.fix: Require positive integer class counts and report support.

findings.summary: StratifiedKFold is explained but never executed or checked for per-fold class support.
findings.fix: Build real folds and report class counts in every train/valid fold.

findings.summary: Plain StratifiedKFold ignores S33 entity-pair grouping and can reintroduce endpoint leakage while balancing labels.
findings.fix: Use group-aware stratification/custom pair-endpoint grouping when unseen-entity generalization is the estimand.

findings.summary: The prose says stratification keeps the same class proportion in every fold; in practice it is approximate subject to discrete counts.
findings.fix: Say approximately the same proportion and retain absolute-support checks.

findings.summary: prevalence(pos,n) accepts impossible counts and divides by zero for n=0.
findings.fix: Validate n>0 and 0<=pos<=n.

findings.summary: accuracy_enough=False is another literal rather than an executable prevalence-aware report gate.
findings.fix: Require base rate/support plus queue metrics in validate_imbalance_report.

findings.summary: brier_mean silently truncates with zip, divides by len(ps), accepts empty/mismatched vectors and probabilities outside [0,1].
findings.fix: Validate sample alignment, binary labels, finite probabilities in [0,1] and non-empty support.

findings.summary: All bins are half-open; the final [0.7,1.0) omits p=1.0 even though calibrate_affine clips outputs to exactly 1.0.
findings.fix: Make the final bin right-inclusive while keeping internal bins half-open.

findings.summary: A single bin with abs(mean_p-freq)<=0.1 is elevated to calibrated=True with no support; chance agreement can certify a globally uncalibrated model.
findings.fix: Call it bin_aligned and assess multiple bins with support before a model-level calibration verdict.

findings.summary: Brier is framed too close to a calibration-only signal; it combines reliability/calibration, resolution/discriminative power and uncertainty.
findings.fix: State this limitation and use reliability curves for calibration shape.

findings.summary: The paragraph says the affine map must not be called Platt while the code docstring calls it a simplified Platt implementation.
findings.fix: Rename it explicitly as an affine didactic calibrator, not Platt scaling.

findings.summary: a=0.8,b=0.1 and calibrator_set='holdout_v1' are hard-coded; no fitting or split-disjointness is demonstrated.
findings.fix: Fit on an identified calibration split and persist split/model/calibrator provenance.

findings.summary: The calibrator rounds to two decimals before downstream decisions and does not validate finite inputs or monotonic orientation; rounding 0.595 to 0.60 flips a threshold decision.
findings.fix: Keep full precision internally, round only display values and validate finite/monotone calibration parameters.

findings.summary: The prose requires Brier/reliability on data not used to fit calibration, but canonical code never performs that evaluation or a final test.
findings.fix: Add calibration-fit and independent calibration-eval/final-test stages.

findings.summary: choose_thr tunes directly on labeled rows without threshold-validation/final-test provenance; same-set reporting would be selection-biased.
findings.fix: Tune threshold on a named validation/CV artifact and evaluate the frozen policy once on untouched final test.

findings.summary: choose_thr does not validate vector lengths, binary labels, finite scores, nonnegative costs, capacity or no-feasible-policy cases; capacity=0 returns None/inf.
findings.fix: Fail closed on invalid inputs and explicit no-feasible policy.

findings.summary: The optimizer always rejects n_review==0, which can force a dominated policy when no review is legitimately cheapest.
findings.fix: Include threshold>max(score) as no-review or declare/validate min_reviews>0 as a business constraint.

findings.summary: Equal-cost thresholds silently keep the first/lower threshold, often creating more review load without a documented preference.
findings.fix: Version an explicit tie-break such as lower load, higher recall or higher threshold.

findings.summary: thr-v1 is a literal not bound to model, calibrator, cost matrix, capacity, prevalence or tuning snapshot.
findings.fix: Persist an immutable ThresholdManifest with hashes and policy parameters.

findings.summary: T4-A optimizes one threshold, then T4-B replaces it with unrelated low=.3/high=.7 defaults; the final policy does not use the optimized thr-vN.
findings.fix: Optimize/version low/high as the same decision-policy artifact and explain their relation to cost/capacity.

findings.summary: decide accepts NaN and inverted bands; NaN becomes abstain and low>high is not rejected.
findings.fix: Validate finite score and 0<=low<high<=1 before routing.

findings.summary: The opening says the gray band exists so a human decides, but decide() returns abstain while review is reserved for >high; abstain routing and capacity consumption are undefined.
findings.fix: Define operational destinations for skip/review/abstain and count all human-routed cases toward capacity.

findings.summary: The heading promises slices and sensitivity but code only counts binary-threshold flips; no slice table exists and force_label=False is hard-coded.
findings.fix: Compute support/P/R/cost/abstain-rate by slice and sensitivity of the full policy.

findings.summary: Abstention is first-class but coverage/abstain-rate/performance-on-decided cases are absent.
findings.fix: Report n_skip/n_review/n_abstain, coverage and consumed review capacity.

findings.summary: Specificity, headcount, slice, reliability, Platt, isotonic, resampling, holdout and PR-AUC are introduced unevenly; specificity is used causally without definition.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish-first meanings and the causal relationship each term serves.

findings.summary: T3-B calls calibration-fit/evaluation separation a way to avoid training-serving skew; this is evaluation leakage/in-sample optimism, not train-serving parity.
findings.fix: Use the correct leakage term and reserve train-serving skew for transformation/distribution parity.

findings.summary: REJECT_UNCALIBRATED is absolute although S34 itself notes an uncalibrated score can still rank usefully; calibration is mandatory only when the product interprets scores probabilistically or makes it an explicit gate.
findings.fix: State that ranking-only use need not imply probability, while CP-N3-B explicitly requires calibrated probabilities for its decision policy.

findings.summary: Theory intentionally uses different tiny fixtures but never closes with one versioned prediction table flowing through metrics, calibration, threshold and abstention.
findings.fix: Keep hand-calculation mini-demos, then add one integrated out-of-sample evidence table before the section gate.

rejected_findings.claim: n0/n1 is inherently the wrong class-weight formula
rejected_findings.reason: Relative binary weights {0:1,1:n0/n1} are proportional to balanced class weights; the defect is missing validation/fit integration.

rejected_findings.claim: Tiny handcrafted metric datasets are invalid
rejected_findings.reason: They are defensible for hand calculation if not used as performance evidence and followed by an integrated out-of-sample gate.

rejected_findings.claim: Half-open reliability bins are inherently wrong
rejected_findings.reason: They prevent double-counting internal boundaries; only the final bin must handle p=1.0.

rejected_findings.claim: An affine didactic calibrator is forbidden because it is not Platt
rejected_findings.reason: It can teach the mapping mechanism if named honestly; the defects are false naming, no fitting/evaluation and unsafe numerical policy.

rejected_findings.claim: Accuracy must never be reported under imbalance
rejected_findings.reason: Accuracy is valid context; it is insufficient as the sole operational metric.
Abstention is legitimate; routing, coverage, capacity and versioning are the missing contracts.

usable: precision/recall/F1 formulas under validated binary counts
PR/AP and queue metrics are useful under rare positives
resampling belongs only in training folds
prevalence is necessary context for precision
Brier is a proper probabilistic score and reliability compares predicted vs observed frequency
calibration fit, threshold tuning and final test are distinct stages
threshold is product policy constrained by cost/capacity
abstention can be first-class without implying fraud/relationship truth
misconception_risk: individual ordering of tied scores = valid AP
rounded probability is safe for decisions
